title: Pressure gauge class 1.6: why error is calculated from the scale, not from the reading
description: Analysis of a pressure gauge selection error: the percentage of the upper scale value was mistakenly taken as a percentage of the reading. Calculation and a ready remark for procurement.
seo_title: Pressure gauge error class 1.6: percentage of scale or reading
seo_description: Scale 0–2.5 MPa and class 1.6 give a limit of ±0.040 MPa. Why calculation from the current reading creates erroneous approval of the instrument.
content:
The entry "accuracy class 1.6" cannot be automatically read as an error of ±1.6 percent of the current reading. If the description of the selected pressure gauge defines it relative to the upper scale value, the calculation is made from that value. With a scale from zero to 2.5 MPa, the result is ±0.040 MPa even at the point 0.20 MPa. An erroneous calculation from the reading gives ±0.0032 MPa and creates a false basis to accept the instrument for a more demanding task.

What exactly is compared in procurement

Let us examine a conditional offer for pressure gauge M-7 for a documentary check of a boiler parameter. The buyer's task requires that the stated permissible error limit in the agreed conditions not exceed ±0.010 MPa at the working point 0.20 MPa. This is a specific procurement condition, not a universal requirement for all boilers or pressure instruments.

The manufacturer's appendix for the proposed execution states a scale of 0–2.5 MPa and a limit of ±1.6 percent of the upper scale value. The belonging of the appendix to execution M-7 is confirmed. For simplicity, the example conditions coincide with the stated conditions of this characteristic; additional temperature influences are not calculated here. Thus the initial task is fully defined: to compare the stated characteristic with the numerical requirement.

The procurement specialist wrote: "At point 0.20 MPa the deviation is no more than 0.20 × 1.6 / 100 = 0.0032 MPa; condition met." The multiplication arithmetic is correct, but a different percentage base was chosen. In the M-7 characteristic there is no promise to calculate the percentage from each current point.

We check two calculations and obtain a definite conclusion

Percentage baseCalculationComparison with task
Erroneously: reading 0.20 MPa0.20 × 0.016 = 0.0032 MPaCreates false confirmation of the 0.010 limit
Per description: top of scale 2.5 MPa2.5 × 0.016 = 0.040 MPaThe stated boundary is four times the required one

The result is no longer reduced to a request to collect additional data: the M-7 offer does not confirm the agreed requirement by the stated limit. The buyer must remove the positive approval based on 0.0032 MPa. To return to selection, a different justified option or a properly changed task is needed, not a new signature under the previous calculation.

At the same time, from the result one cannot conclude that a specific specimen necessarily errs by exactly 0.040 MPa. The permissible error limit sets the boundary of the characteristic, not the measured correction of this specimen. One cannot subtract 0.040 from each reading or declare the whole instrument defective just because it does not fit a stricter procurement condition.

Why such an error is especially noticeable in the lower part of the scale

For the characteristic considered, the absolute boundary 0.040 MPa remains the same at different readings in the stated region. Relative to the point 0.20 MPa it is 20 percent, and relative to 2.00 MPa it is 2 percent. This does not turn class 1.6 into two different classes. What changes is the ratio of one absolute boundary to two different readings.

WIKA's primary explanation of pressure gauge accuracy classes defines such a characteristic through the full scale value and gives its own example of its calculation. It confirms the meaning of the percentage base. The M-7 numbers and the buyer's requirement in our analysis are conditional; they are not the passport of a specific WIKA model.

The inscription with a percentage should be read in full. For an electronic transducer, the manufacturer may set a different base, range, combination of several components and conditions of validity. The given formula cannot be transferred to any line "accuracy, percent". For a scale with a nonzero start, it is also important to distinguish the upper value and the difference of limits: in our example the start is zero, so this separate ambiguity does not arise.

Indication of a fine scale division also does not replace the error characteristic: the ability to distinguish close marks by itself does not promise corresponding instrument accuracy.

Ready remark for approval of execution

For M-7, the appendix establishes ±1.6 percent of the upper scale value 0–2.5 MPa. This is ±0.040 MPa, not ±0.0032 MPa calculated from the working point 0.20 MPa. The task condition of a limit no more than ±0.010 MPa is not confirmed by the proposed characteristic. We ask to replace the positive approval with selection of an execution with a confirmed limit for the specified task and conditions of use.

A narrower scale alone is not yet a ready solution: requirements for permissible regimes, compatibility and instrument purpose are preserved separately. Here a specific erroneous basis of selection is corrected, not a permission issued to replace an installed pressure gauge. If such a calculation has already entered the boiler set, send to NPI "Nedra" the specific characteristic and the requirement with which it was compared.
